initial_requirements: Public health organizations need an outbreak management system to support investigation, monitoring, analysis, and reporting during disease outbreaks, bioterrorism incidents, and other health events. Investigators should be able to collect information about cases, contacts, exposures, specimens, and interventions, connect related entities and events, and use the resulting information to identify and contain a health threat while protecting sensitive data.

messages.content:
Hello, I’m GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about the PHIN Outbreak Management System to help ensure we understand the needed scope and requirements clearly.

Before we begin, are you in line with this interview’s scope, or do your expectations differ?

Yes, I’m aligned with that scope. We’re focused on supporting outbreak investigation, monitoring, analysis, and reporting, with enough flexibility to handle related public health events while keeping sensitive information protected.
Thank you. To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?

I’m representing the public health program side for this system, so I’m thinking from the perspective of investigators and program managers who will use it during outbreaks. My role is to make sure the system supports real investigation workflows, reporting needs, and data protection requirements.
Thanks, that helps. Could you describe the current process or systems you use today for outbreak investigation, monitoring, and reporting?

Right now it’s pretty fragmented. Teams are often working out of spreadsheets, email, shared drives, and sometimes separate surveillance or case management systems, so a lot of the linking between cases, contacts, exposures, and specimens happens manually. Reporting also tends to be assembled by hand, which takes time and makes it harder to keep everything consistent when the situation is changing quickly.
What current processes do you want to change or improve, or what main features are you hoping to get from this project?

We want to reduce the manual work of stitching information together and make it easier to see relationships between people, places, events, and lab results in one place. I’d also like faster situational awareness through dashboards or summaries, plus better role-based access so sensitive investigation details are only visible to the right people.

So the main features I’ve heard are: connecting related cases, contacts, exposures, specimens, and events in one place; dashboards or summaries for situational awareness; and role-based access controls to protect sensitive information.

Are there any other features you would like to see in this project?

Yes, we’d also want strong search and filtering, because investigators need to find records quickly during a fast-moving event. It would be important to track interventions and follow-up actions over time, and to have audit history so we can see who changed what and when. We’d also likely need import and export capabilities, since we may still have to share data with other systems or partners.
Based on what you’ve described, do you think secure messaging or notifications for task follow-up should also be included?

Yes, I think that would be very useful. Investigators and supervisors need timely reminders when a follow-up, specimen, or interview is due, and secure messaging would help coordinate without relying on email for sensitive details. The exact form is not fixed yet, but some kind of in-system notification or alerting should be in scope.

So far, the main features seem to be:
- linked management of cases, contacts, exposures, specimens, interventions, and events
- dashboards and summaries for situational awareness
- role-based access control
- search and filtering
- intervention and follow-up tracking
- audit history
- import/export
- in-system notifications or alerts
- secure messaging

Which of these should be highest priority for the first release?

For the first release, I’d put linked management of the core entities, role-based access control, and search/filtering at the top. Those are the basics investigators need to actually use the system during an outbreak. After that, dashboards, follow-up tracking, and audit history would be very important, with notifications and secure messaging probably following if we need to phase things in.
Please elaborate on what you want the linked management of the core entities to accomplish.

It should let investigators create and maintain a single view of how a case connects to contacts, exposures, specimens, and interventions, instead of treating each as separate records. We need to be able to add relationships as they’re discovered, update them over time, and see the chain of evidence or activity that supports the investigation. Ideally, it should also make it easy to tell when two records may actually belong to the same real-world person or event so we can avoid duplication.
